nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Bare NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: Bare NiFe LDH nanosheets were synthesized via the hydrothermal method on nickel foam substrate (detailed procedure in Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: bare NiFe LDH and S doping NiFe LDH (denoted as S-NiFe LDH) were synthesized via the hydrothermal method (see Supporting Information for details)

nodes.name: S-doped Hydrothermal Synthesis of NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: S-doped NiFe LDH (S-NiFe LDH) was synthesized via hydrothermal method by adding varying amounts of Na₂S₂O₃·5H₂O to NiFe LDH synthesis. The optimal S doping was achieved with 50 mg Na₂S₂O₃·5H₂O to balance electronic regulation effect while avoiding formation of nickel sulfide (detailed procedure in Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: the S doping amount was adjusted by varying the added amount of Na₂S₂O₃·5H₂O... corresponding to 50 mg Na₂S₂O₃·5H₂O

nodes.description: OER performance evaluation in 1 M KOH after CV activation
nodes.source_text: The activated S-NiFe LDH requires an overpotential of 259 mV at 100 mA cm⁻²... The S-NiFe LDH catalyst is also relatively stable, showing no significant potential fluctuation for the 360 h test at high current densities (Figure 4b).

nodes.description: OER performance evaluation in 1 M KOH after CV activation
nodes.source_text: the OER activity of S-NiFe LDH is much better than that of NiFe LDH at all current densities. After the 1000th CV cycle... the activity of undoped NiFe LDH significantly deteriorated.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of S-NiFe LDH shows no evident peaks of nickel sulfate or sulfide, and (003) peak shows no shift after S introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of S-NiFe LDH shows no evident peaks of nickel sulfate or sulfide (Figure S4b, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Stretching vibration of interlayer CO_3^2- is unchanged in S-NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the stretching vibration of interlayer CO_3^2- is unchanged in the infrared spectra (Figure S4c, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: S 2p XPS peaks at 162.4 eV and 164.3 eV attributed to S-metal bonding; peak at ≈169.5 eV from surface oxidized S atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the S 2p X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum (Figure S4d, Supporting Information), the characteristic peaks at 162.4 and 164.3 eV are attributed to the bonding of sulfur with metal atoms. In addition, the peak at ≈169.5 eV is attributed to S atoms of catalyst surface that were partially oxidized during the hydrothermal treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: S-NiFe LDH shows thick layer of cross-linked ultrathin nanosheets covering nickel foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, a thick layer of cross-linked nanosheets covers the surface of nickel foam substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of both catalysts similar to Ni(OH)_2 indicating mainly Ni^{2+}; S-NiFe LDH shows weak negative shift and weaker white-line peak at ≈8351 eV indicating higher 3d occupancy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge spectra (Figure 2e) shows that the Ni state in the prepared S-NiFe LDH and NiFe LDH is similar to Ni(OH)_2, suggesting Ni mainly exists in the valence state of Ni^{2+}. However, the Ni K-edge of S-NiFe LDH presents a weak negative shift compared to NiFe LDH... The main characteristic peak located at ≈8351 eV in the Ni K-edge XANES spectra is the white-line peak, which is weaker in S-NiFe LDH than that of NiFe LDH and Ni(OH)_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows peaks at 1.59 Å and 2.73 Å for Ni-O and Ni-M bonds; S-NiFe LDH shows additional peak at 1.07 Å indicating distorted Ni octahedron.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra (Figure 2f; Figure S6b, Supporting Information), two characteristic peaks at 1.59 and 2.73 Å are ascribed to Ni-O and Ni-M (M stands for Ni or Fe) bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform analysis shows enhanced scattering at ≈6.6 Å^-1 assigned to increased Ni-M coordination in S-NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure 2g, the two maxima centered at 1.59 and 2.73 Å correspond to the Ni-O and Ni-M bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Ni 2p XPS shows increase of Ni^{3+}/Ni^{2+} ratio after CV cycles, more pronounced in S-NiFe LDH; Fe 2p maintains Fe^{3+} state throughout.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectra (Figure 2h), the valence state of Ni partially changes from the initial Ni^{2+} to Ni^{3+}, and Ni^{3+} dominates after the 40th cycle. Correspondingly, the deconvoluted Ni 2p region of NiFe LDH also exhibits an apparent increase in the intensity ratio of Ni^{3+} to Ni^{2+} after the CV cycles (Figure 2i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows transformation from Ni(OH)_2 (peaks at 443 and 526 cm^-1) to NiOOH (peaks at 471 and 548 cm^-1) faster and to higher concentration in S-NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the operando Raman spectral evolution in Figure 3b; Figure S12, Supporting Information, the dynamic reconstruction process can be divided into two stages...

nodes.characterization_summary: 2D correlation Raman spectroscopy confirms phase transition from hydroxides to oxyhydroxides, more pronounced in S-NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further demonstrate the existence of a phase transition from hydroxides to oxyhydroxides, the 2D correlation Raman spectroscopy (2D-CORS) was performed.

nodes.characterization_summary: 2D-CORS synchronous spectrum shows auto-peaks at ≈474 cm^{-1} (Ni^{III}-OH) and 558 cm^{-1} (Ni^{III}-O); S-NiFe LDH shows stronger 474 cm^{-1} auto-peak indicating more extensive phase change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The synchronous spectrum shows two auto-peaks at ≈474 and 558 cm^{-1} (Figure 3d), corresponding to Ni^{III}-OH and Ni^{III}-O, respectively. The auto-peak at ≈474 cm^{-1} is significantly stronger in S-NiFe LDH compared to NiFe LDH (Figure 3e).
